question: HRCT of the temporal bone (bone-window algorithm, 0.5–1 mm slices) is the preferred first-line imaging modality for CSOM because it precisely delineates the bony anatomy of the middle ear, mastoid, ossicular chain, and tegmen — information that directly guides surgical planning.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The temporal bone is predominantly bone; CT with bone-window algorithm gives unparalleled spatial resolution for bony detail. MRI is complementary, not first-line, for CSOM.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. HRCT temporal bone in bone-window algorithm is the workhorse for CSOM evaluation. It defines the extent of disease, ossicular erosion, tegmen/sigmoid plate integrity, and presence of cholesteatoma soft tissue. MRI is added when intracranial complications or soft-tissue characterisation (cholesteatoma vs. granulation) is needed.
